name: cholesky
description: Representative ATen signature (not an exclusive ABI): aten::cholesky(Tensor self, bool upper=False) -> Tensor. All registered schemas supplied for this operator, verbatim: aten::cholesky(Tensor self, bool upper=False) -> Tensor; aten::cholesky.out(Tensor self, bool upper=False, *, Tensor(a!) out) -> Tensor(a!). Original Gems pytest owns the full overload, keyword, return, error, mutation and aliasing contract; the representative signature is not exclusive and tests must not be narrowed to it. Semantics derived from the supplied pytest and benchmark, measured on the active backend rather than asserted for every backend or version: factors a Hermitian positive-definite matrix, or a batch of matrices with rank >= 2 and equal last two dimensions, into a lower (upper=False, the default) or an upper (upper=True) triangular factor. Only the triangle selected by upper is read; the opposite triangle is ignored, non-finite entries included; only the real part of the diagonal is read, so an imaginary diagonal part is ignored. The measured dtype domain is float32, float64, complex64 and complex128: float32 and complex64 are exercised unconditionally, while float64 and complex128 are exercised only when the backend's static fp64 capability flag is set, and the negative dtype cases are populated only for the NVIDIA vendor, so unsupported dtypes raise (RuntimeError/TypeError) is established for that vendor only. The factorization is not in-place: no element of the input storage, inside or outside a view, is modified. Rank < 2 and non-square shapes raise (RuntimeError/TypeError), while non-positive-definite inputs (negative definite, singular, late minors, mixed batch), nan and -inf diagonal entries, and nan/+inf entries in the read triangle raise torch._C._LinAlgError (a RuntimeError subclass); a +inf diagonal entry does not raise and yields a non-finite factor whose nan positions are compared with an equal_nan comparison. Overload-dependent behavior not expressed by this single-overload model: the registered keyword-only variant aten::cholesky.out(self, upper=False, *, out) writes into the supplied buffer, returns that same tensor, mutates only out, and is exercised directly by pytest through flag_gems.cholesky(inp, upper, out=out) with `assert res_ret is out`; the default overload has no mutation and no aliasing. The schema default upper=False is copied verbatim as the JSON boolean false (no non-JSON default rendering is involved).
